name: Teen Harbour
tagline: Support a struggling teen with a plan, not just worry
about: Teen Harbour helps parents of teenagers with anxiety, low mood or self-harm build a safety plan, find and prepare for therapy, ask school for support, and get through exam season and bad nights.
persona: You are a youth-mental-health clinician speaking to parents: warm, plain-spoken, evidence-based, clear about crisis lines, and never diagnosing from a message.

onboarding.title: You don't have to guess
onboarding.subtitle: A few details let us tailor the plan and point to the right services.
bullets: A safety plan you build together

tools.title: Safety plan
tools.subtitle: Build it together, tonight

inputs.label: What tends to set things off
inputs.placeholder: exam results, arguments with Dad, late nights scrolling

inputs.label: People they trust
inputs.placeholder: cousin Jess, Mr Patel at school

tools.prompt: Draft a collaborative safety plan for the profile's teen with triggers: {triggers} and trusted people: {people}. Sections: a kv using the standard safety-plan headings (warning signs, coping things I can do alone, people and places that distract me, people I can ask for help, professionals and crisis lines for the profile's country, making my environment safer), a quote with how to introduce the plan to the teen so it doesn't feel like punishment, a checklist of what to make safer at home (medicines, sharps, alcohol), and a callout on what to do if there is immediate risk tonight.

tools.title: Find & prep for therapy
tools.subtitle: Types, cost, first session

inputs.label: Preferences
inputs.placeholder: female therapist, evenings, not CBT again

tools.prompt: Guide a parent to therapy for the profile's teen: route {route}, budget {budget} per session, preferences {prefs}. Sections: a table (Therapy type | Good for | Typical wait | Typical cost in the profile's country), steps to get a referral or vet a private therapist (credentials to check, questions for the first call), a checklist of what to prepare for the first session, and a callout on confidentiality between therapist, teen and parent.

tools.title: Ask the school
tools.subtitle: Support request letter

inputs.label: What's happening at school
inputs.placeholder: panic before assessments, missed 8 days this term

tools.prompt: Situation: {situation}. Asking for: {ask}. Sections: a quote with a complete email to the pastoral lead or counsellor (under 250 words, factual, requests a meeting and specific adjustments), bullets of adjustments schools commonly grant for mental-health needs in the profile's country and the formal routes (for example a 504 plan, SEN support or an individual healthcare plan), a checklist of documents to bring, and a callout on what to do if the school is unresponsive.

tools.title: Exam-season plan
tools.subtitle: Pressure without collapse

inputs.label: What you're seeing
inputs.placeholder: not sleeping, crying at revision, says she'll fail everything

tools.prompt: Plan exam season for the profile's teen: {exams}. Current signs: {signs}. Sections: a table (Week | Parent's job | What to stop doing | Check-in question), steps for a panic-before-exam protocol the teen can run alone, bullets on sleep, food and movement basics that matter more than extra revision hours, a quote with what to say the night before the first exam, and a callout on signs that this is beyond exam stress.

tools.title: After a bad night
tools.subtitle: Repair, rest, next steps

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: found messages about not wanting to be here; we talked till 2am

tools.prompt: After: {what}. Sections: a callout first on whether this needs same-day professional contact and exactly who to call in the profile's country, steps for today (rest, supervision, who else to tell, what to say to siblings), a quote with a short message to send the teen this morning, bullets for the parent's own support, and a kv of what to observe over the next 72 hours.

disclaimer: This is general information, not therapy or medical advice. If your teen is in immediate danger, call emergency services or your local crisis line now.
